He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]]. ==Early life and high school career== Alexander grew up in [[Oklahoma City, Oklahoma]], and attended [[Heritage Hall School]].{{cite web|title=Heritage Hall's Trey Alexander tells why he decommitted from Auburn|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2021/04/23/heritage-halls-trey-alexander-tells-why-he-decommitted-auburn-tigers/7352473002/|work=[[The Oklahoman]]|date=April 23, 2021|access-date=February 16, 2023}} He was named the Oklahoma Gatorade Player of the Year after averaging 23.6 points, 8.7 rebounds, four assists, and 2.1 steals per game as a senior.{{cite web|title=Creighton commit Trey Alexander is Oklahoma's Gatorade player of the year|url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/creighton-commit-trey-alexander-is-oklahomas-gatorade-player-of-the-year/article_05dc8e70-c54e-11eb-9afb-5ba3ac5103ad.html|work=[[Omaha World-Herald]]|date=June 4, 2021|access-date=February 16, 2023}} Alexander was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]]. In November 2020, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] over offers from [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]], and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Green|title=4-star 2021 shooting guard Trey Alexander commits to Auburn|url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2020/11/4-star-2021-shooting-guard-trey-alexander-commits-to-auburn.html|website=[[AL.com]]|date=November 12, 2020|access-date=February 16, 2023}} Alexander decommitted from the program at the end of his senior season.{{cite web|title=Four-star Auburn basketball signee Trey Alexander reopens recruitment|url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/auburn/2021/04/22/auburn-basketball-recruiting-trey-alexander-decommits-bruce-pearl/7336499002/|work=[[Montgomery Advertiser]]|date=April 22, 2021|access-date=February 16, 2023}} He later signed to play for [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].{{cite web|title=Creighton basketball: Heritage Hall's Trey Alexander commits to Bluejays|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2021/06/02/creighton-basketball-heritage-halls-trey-alexander-commits-bluejays/7507091002/|work=[[The Oklahoman]]|date=June 2, 2021|access-date=February 16, 2023}} ==College career== Alexander played in all 35 of Creighton's games during his freshman season and was named to the [[Big East Conference]] All-Freshman team after averaging 7.4 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game.{{cite web|title=Who are the top college basketball players from Oklahoma high schools?|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/01/14/who-are-the-top-college-basketball-players-from-oklahoma-high-schools/69805246007/|work=[[The Oklahoman]]|date=January 14, 2023|access-date=February 16, 2023}} He became the Bluejays' starting point guard after [[Ryan Nembhard]] suffered a season-ending injury.{{cite web|title=As Trey Alexander moves into new role, Ryan Nembhard ready to help from Creighton's bench|url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/as-trey-alexander-moves-into-new-role-ryan-nembhard-ready-to-help-from-creightons-bench/article_d69416cc-992a-11ec-a568-6fda2a0b4a1d.html|work=[[Omaha World-Herald]]|date=March 4, 2022|access-date=February 17, 2023}} Alexander averaged 11.6 points, 4.3 assists, and four assists during the final eight games of the season.{{cite web|title=The emergence of "combo guard" Trey Alexander could be key on a loaded Creighton roster|url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/the-emergence-of-combo-guard-trey-alexander-could-be-key-on-a-loaded-creighton-roster/article_beac8a2a-497f-11ed-9500-c7b0a5a5a0e1.html|work=[[Omaha World-Herald]]|date=October 12, 2022|access-date=February 17, 2023}} Alexander entered his sophomore season as Creighton's starting shooting guard.{{cite web|title=As starters shine, Creighton basketball's low-scoring bench continues to evolve|url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/as-starters-shine-creighton-basketball-s-low-scoring-bench-continues-to-evolve/article_f0bfe4ce-a6ec-11ed-a6d6-27d5bdbe50c4.html|work=[[Omaha World-Herald]]|date=February 8, 2023|access-date=February 17, 2023}} ==Professional career== === Denver Nuggets (2024–2025) === After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Alexander joined the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=DENVER NUGGETS ANNOUNCE 2024 NBA SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER AND MINI-CAMP SCHEDULE|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-announce-2024-nba-summer-league-roster-and-mini-camp-schedule|website=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}} and on July 10, 2024, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the team.{{cite web|title=NUGGETS SIGN HALL AND ALEXANDER TO TWO-WAY CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-hall-and-alexander-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2024|access-date=July 19, 2024}} === New Orleans Pelicans (2025–2026) === On July 3, 2025, Alexander signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] on a two-way contract.{{Cite web |title=Trey Alexander {{!}} Guard {{!}} New Orleans Pelicans {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1641725/trey-alexander |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=NBA |language=en}} === Utah Jazz (2026–present) === On July 7, 2026, Alexander signed with the [[Utah Jazz]] on a two-way contract.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-trey-alexander-to-two-way-contract|title=Utah Jazz Sign Trey Alexander to Two-Way Contract|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2026}} ==Personal life== Alexander is the son of Steve and Pamela Alexander. He has one sister. His uncle, DeAngelo Alexander, played basketball at [[University of Oklahoma]] and [[UNC Charlotte]] his other uncle, Xavier Alexander, played basketball at [[George Washington University]].{{cite web |title=Trey Alexander - 2023-24 - Men's Basketball |url=https://gocreighton.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/trey-alexander/7808 |website=Creighton University Athletics |access-date=30 October 2025 |language=en}} Alexander and [[Mike Conley Jr.]] are cousins on his mother's side.{{cite web |last1=Jourdan |first1=Cameron |date=January 31, 2020 |title=Hoop dreams: Basketball a family affair for
